passage:
A red telephone booth stood unused on a street corner. The city wanted to remove it.
Residents suggested turning it into a mini information center. They placed maps, emergency numbers, local history notes, and a shelf for free books inside.
Tourists began stopping there. Children liked stepping inside and imagining a time before mobile phones.
The booth no longer made calls, but it still connected people to the neighborhood.
Reuse gave it a second life without pretending the first life continued.
Some objects survive best when communities allow them to change purpose while keeping their recognizable shape.
